title: Add support for configuration path relocation on Unix
description:
Get the installation prefix from the program dir. We have code
to obtain the directory where the executable resides for all
platforms we support, Linux, BSDs, Apple, etc.

On more obscure platforms where this isn't true (POSIX does not
define any standard interfaces for this) we need to fallback on
using a hard-coded installation prefix, like we have been doing
until now.

The path relocation allows the whole installation tree to be moved
without having to recompile the program. But note there are other
requirements for shared libraries to have full support for relocation.
This is only partial support.

We now use a header to pass the relative path definitions to avoid
excessively long compilation command lines as the number of #defines
increases.

notes.body:
macOS app bundles have an "installation path", as everything's under the top-level .app directory.  As far as I know, you can move Wireshark.app somewhere other than /Applications and it should be launchable.

I think the same applies on Windows, with the top-level Wireshark directory having everything under it.

Is this for applications installed in subdirectories of /usr or /usr/local or..., in the traditional UN\*X style?

Right, Windows builds and macOS app bundles already have support for this, AFAIK. So this brings parity to other platforms.

This allows moving the installation tree without breaking the application. The main use case would be zipping the folder in one machine and unzipping it in another and have everything work seamlessly.

> So this brings parity to other platforms.

I guess other platforms and packaging systems that use /opt/{application}/{files} would also work already, but platforms and packaging systems that use /opt/{bin, lib,etc,...} would require this change.  (I thinkk I've seen both flavors of /opt used.)

Another use case would be for [AppImage](https://docs.appimage.org/reference/best-practices.html#binaries-must-not-use-compiled-in-absolute-paths), which ends up running from a semi-random path. Snap and FlatPak might do something similar.

`suite_clopts.case_tshark_dump_glossaries` is failing on macOS as well. `appbundle_dir` is set at the top of `init_plugin_dir` but we don't reach the `#ifdef __APPLE__` block.

...which is because `running_in_build_directory_flag` is set. 

Is there any way that we could simplify the logic in the various `init_xxx_dir` routines? For example, would it make sense to have a single set of platform ifdefs that defined regular and "build directory" datafile, extcap, plugin, etc paths relative to the program directory?
!9621 fixes the issue here on macOS.
